newsitem.title: FRANCE: GOLF-PARNEVIK EDGES AHEAD WITH LAST HOLE BIRDIE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-PARNEVIK EDGES AHEAD WITH LAST HOLE BIRDIE.

text.p: Jesper Parnevik curled in a 60 feet birdie putt at the last hole to snatch a one shot lead from holder Colin Montgomerie in the third round of the Lancome Trophy on Saturday.

The Swede's four-under-par 66 was matched by the Scot, who appeared set for first place himself until he bogeyed the 209 yards final hole after his tee shot left him with a bad lie in a greenside bunker.
Then Parnevik, playing behind, rolled in his swinging putt from just off the front of the green for his nine-under total of 201, one better than Montgomerie.
Ian Woosnam, Montgomerie's rival for the European Order of Merit title, could only manage a 70 and was four shots off the lead after sharing it overnight.
With Woosnam on five-under were fellow Britons Jamie Spence, the first round leader who carded a 67, and Ross Drummond, who shot 69.
Parnevik, now a U.S. Tour player, is ineligible for Ryder Cup points in Europe but Montgomerie insisted that he will be needed for next year's defence against the Americans.
"I'm mightily impressed by Parnevik. He's one of the top five players in Europe," Montgomerie said.
Montgomerie pointed to this weekend's President's Cup in which the Americans lead an International team containing no Europeans by 7-1/2 points to 2-1/2 to justify his support for Parnevik.
"The international team is as strong if not stronger that we are and they're getting thrashed. We will need our strongest team," he said.
"He should be in the Ryder Cup team, definitely."
Parnevik responded by saying he would like to think he was one of the leading Europeans, "but it's all down to politics, like anything else".
The Swede, runner-up in the 1994 British Open, has committed himself to playing predominantly on the U.S. Tour rather than trying to qualify in Europe.
Parnevik said he was surprised at his score because he was up all night with food poisoning.
"I'd have taken a 70, especially after a bogey at the second hole," he said. "I felt I played sloppy golf today. I was very tired."
But he birdied the next two and the eighth and ninth, lost a shot at the 14th before a birdie at 16 set up his glorious final putt.
Montgomerie was quickly out of the blocks with birdies at the first two holes, which he bogeyed in Friday's round, and the fourth, where he made a 30-foot putt.
He made further birdies at the 10th and 17th before his dropped shot at the last.
"One behind is fine. I'm quite confident in what I'm doing," said the Scot, who regained the Order of Merit lead from Woosnam with his record-breaking victory last Sunday in the European Masters.
Woosnam has been troubled by a bad back but said that had no bearing on his round. "I just didn't drive the ball well today," he said.
